items.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: In fact Herbie Hancock just came out with a record

ctx.x: Yes. I was a product of the era when everybody else went to Elvis and the Beatles. And I stayed with the big bands, and I stayed with Ellington and Basie and I never moved off of mainstream jazz. Rhythm and melody. I really like the standards. Even the new jazz is really not so much my preference as it is to hear a Gershwin or a Berlin or an Ellington or a Basie tune and hear it done the original way as well as hearing it done today. And I do a lot of that. I call it mixing and matching. Doing the same song done…

I’ve often wondered if we are writing, since the ‘40s especially, is anybody writing standards since then you know? In fact Herbie Hancock just came out with a record and I forget the exact title of it, but what he did was he found what he thought were going to be the standards to come. And he did some more modern tunes but treated them as jazz tunes I guess.

Well I think those probably will be standards for our children and maybe our grand- children, but I think for me, certainly for me personally as well as for me collectively, the Tin Pan Alley songs are what America is all about. Those will always be loved songs because they’re just part of America.
